# Bartib

Bartib is an easy to use time tracking tool for the command line. It saves a log of all tracked activities as a plaintext file and allows you to create flexible reports.

Usage examples

Start a new activity:

  bartib start -d "Description of the activity" -p "Project Name"

Stop the running activity:

  bartib stop

Continue the most recent activity:

  bartib continue

List today's activities:

  bartib list --today

Report for today:

  bartib report --today

Configuration

Bartib records activities in a plaintext log file. You can either pass the file explicitly with the -f/--file option, or set the BARTIB_FILE environment variable to point to your log file. Example:

  export BARTIB_FILE="/home/username/activities.bartib"

If the file does not exist, Bartib will create it when you start tracking.

Installation

Download a prebuilt executable from the project's releases and place it in a directory on your PATH (for example: ~/bin). Bartib may also be available through your distribution's package manager.

Autocompletion

Completion scripts for shells may be provided in the repository's misc/ directory. Source the appropriate script for your shell to enable completion of project and task names.

License

This project is provided under the terms of the LICENSE file in this repository.

#!/bin/bash

_bartib_completions()
{
	local CWORD=${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}
	ALL_PROJECTS=`bartib projects`

	local IFS=$'\n'
	CANDIATE_PROJECTS=($(compgen -W "${ALL_PROJECTS[*]}" -- "$CWORD"))

	if [ ${#CANDIATE_PROJECTS[*]} -eq 0 ]; then
		COMPREPLY=()
	else
		COMPREPLY=($(printf "\"%s\"\n" "${CANDIATE_PROJECTS[@]}"))
	fi
}

complete -F _bartib_completions bartib
=== _bartib (zsh) ===
#compdef bartib

_bartib_tasks() {
    local -a _tasks=($(bartib last | head -n -1 | awk 'BEGIN { a="" } NR > 2 {for (i=2; i <= NF - 1; i++) { if (i != 2) { a=a" "$i; } else { a=$i } } gsub("[\[\]]", "", $1); printf("%s[%s]\n", $1, a)}' | tr '\n' ' '))

    _values "TASK" ${_tasks[@]}
}

_bartib_projects() {
    local -a _projects=($(bartib projects --no-quotes | sort | tr '\n' ' '))

    _values "PROJECTS" ${_projects[@]}
}

_bartib() {
    typeset -A opt_args
    local context state line
    local current_context="${curcontext}"

    _arguments -C \
        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
        '(-v --version)'{-v,--version}'[Prints version information]' \
        '-f[the file in which bartib tracks all the activities]:FILE:_files' \
        '1:bartib commands:->commands' \
        '*:: :->command_arguments'

    case $state in
        commands)
            local commands
            commands=(
                'cancel:cancels all currently running activities',
                'change:changes the current activity',
                'check:checks file and reports parsing errors',
                'continue:continues a previous activity',
                'current:lists all currently running activities',
                'edit:opens the activity log in an editor',
                'help:Prints this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)',
                'last:displays the descriptions and projects of recent activities',
                'list:list recent activities',
                'projects:list all projects',
                'report:reports duration of tracked activities',
                'sanity:checks sanity of bartib log',
                'search:search for existing descriptions and projects',
                'start:starts a new activity',
                'status:shows current status and time reports for today, current week, and current month',
                'stop:stops all currently running activities'
            )
            _describe -t commands 'bartib command' commands
            ;;

        command_arguments)
            case $words[1] in
                cancel)
                    _arguments -C \

    set -l output (bartib projects 2>/dev/null)

    set -l output (bartib last -n 100 2>/dev/null)

end

function __is_last_argument
    argparse --ignore-unknown 's/short=+' 'l/long=+' -- $argv

            set output 1

        if string match --quiet -- "--*" $t

        end

                set output 0
            end
        end
        for l in $_flag_l

                set output 0
            end
        end
    end

out=$(BARTIB_FILE=/tmp/bt/t.txt /workspace/executable list --round "$1" 2>&1 | python3 -c "
import sys,re
d=sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode('utf-8')
for l in d.split(chr(10)):
    p=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',l).replace(chr(160),'_')
    print('   |'+p)
")
echo "$out" | sed 's/^/    /'
SH
chmod +x /tmp/rt.sh
for r in "15M" "1.5h" "60" "m" "h" "15 m" "1h30m" "1x" "1mm" "0" "00m" "07m" "1441m" "1440m" "12h" "1d"; do echo "=== round '$r'"; /tmp/rt.sh "$r"; done

actions.command:
cd /tmp && python3 - <<'PY'
import re
rows=[]
for line in open('/tmp/results.txt'):
    line=line.rstrip('\n')
    if '=>' not in line: continue
    cmd,res=line.split(' => ',1)
    toks=cmd.split(); order=[]; i=0
    while i < len(toks):
        t=toks[i]
        if t=='-d': order.append('D'); i+=2
        elif t=='--from': order.append('F'); i+=2
        elif t=='--to': order.append('X'); i+=2
        else:
            order.append({'--current_week':'cw','--last_week':'lw','--today':'T','--yesterday':'Y'}[t]); i+=1
    res=res.strip()
    if not res: rows.append((order,None,None)); continue
    m=re.match(r"'([^']+)' \| '([^']+)'", res)
    inv={'--current_week':'cw','--last_week':'lw','--today':'T','--yesterday':'Y','--date <DATE>':'D','--from <FROM_DATE>':'F','--to <TO_DATE>':'X'}
    rows.append((order,inv[m.group(1)],inv[m.group(2)]))
DEF=['F','X','D','T','Y','cw','lw']
conf={'F':{'D','T','Y','cw','lw'},'X':{'D','T','Y','cw','lw'},'D':{'T','Y','cw','lw'},'T':{'Y','cw','lw'},'Y':{'cw','lw'},'cw':{'lw'},'lw':set()}
def model(order):
    for a in DEF:
        if a in order:
            cs=[x for x in order if x!=a and x in conf[a]]
            if cs: return a, cs[0]
    return None
ok=0; bad=0
for order,a,b in rows:
    m=model(order)
    if m==(a,b): ok+=1
    else:
        bad+=1
        if bad<15: print("MISMATCH", order, "expected", (a,b), "model", m)
print("ok",ok,"bad",bad,"total",len(rows))
PY

{"command": "cd /tmp && python3 - <<'PY'
import re, collections
rows=[]
for line in open('/tmp/results.txt'):
    line=line.rstrip('\n')
    if '=>' not in line: continue
    cmd,res=line.split(' => ',1)
    toks=cmd.split(); order=[]; i=0
    while i < len(toks):
        t=toks[i]
        if t=='-d': order.append('D'); i+=2
        elif t=='--from': order.append('F'); i+=2
        elif t=='--to': order.append('X'); i+=2
        else:
            order.append({'--current_week':'cw','--last_week':'lw','--today':'T','--yesterday':'Y'}[t]); i+=1
    res=res.strip()
    if not res: rows.append((order,None,None)); continue
    m=re.match(r"'([^']+)' \| '([^']+)'", res)
    inv={'--current_week':'cw','--last_week':'lw','--today':'T','--yesterday':'Y','--date <DATE>':'D','--from <FROM_DATE>':'F','--to <TO_DATE>':'X'}
    rows.append((order,inv[m.group(1)],inv[m.group(2)]))
sets=collections.defaultdict(list)
for order,a,b in rows:
    if a is None or len(order)!=3: continue
    sets[tuple(sorted(order))].append((order,a,b))
for s,items in list(sets.items())[:8]:
    print("=== ", s)
    for order,a,b in items:
        posA=order.index(a); posB=order.index(b)
        print("   ", order, a, b, "posA",posA,"posB",posB)
PY"}

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'PY'
import re, collections
rows=[]
for line in open('/tmp/results.txt'):
    line=line.rstrip('\n')
    if '=>' not in line: continue
    cmd,res=line.split(' => ',1)
    toks=cmd.split(); order=[]; i=0
    while i < len(toks):
        t=toks[i]
        if t=='-d': order.append('D'); i+=2
        elif t=='--from': order.append('F'); i+=2
        elif t=='--to': order.append('X'); i+=2
        else:
            order.append({'--current_week':'cw','--last_week':'lw','--today':'T','--yesterday':'Y'}[t]); i+=1
    res=res.strip()
    if not res: rows.append((order,None,None)); continue
    m=re.match(r"'([^']+)' \| '([^']+)'", res)
    inv={'--current_week':'cw','--last_week':'lw','--today':'T','--yesterday':'Y','--date <DATE>':'D','--from <FROM_DATE>':'F','--to <TO_DATE>':'X'}
    rows.append((order,inv[m.group(1)],inv[m.group(2)]))
sets=collections.defaultdict(list)
for order,a,b in rows:
    if a is None or len(order)!=3: continue
    sets[tuple(sorted(order))].append((order,a,b))
for s,items in list(sets.items())[:8]:
    print("=== ", s)
    for order,a,b in items:
        posA=order.index(a); posB=order.index(b)
        print("   ", order, a, b, "posA",posA,"posB",posB)
PY

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'PY'
import re, collections
rows=[]
for line in open('/tmp/results.txt'):
    line=line.rstrip('\n')
    if '=>' not in line: continue
    cmd,res=line.split(' => ',1)
    toks=cmd.split(); order=[]; i=0
    while i < len(toks):
        t=toks[i]
        if t=='-d': order.append('D'); i+=2
        elif t=='--from': order.append('F'); i+=2
        elif t=='--to': order.append('X'); i+=2
        else:
            order.append({'--current_week':'cw','--last_week':'lw','--today':'T','--yesterday':'Y'}[t]); i+=1
    res=res.strip()
    if not res: rows.append((order,None,None)); continue
    m=re.match(r"'([^']+)' \| '([^']+)'", res)
    inv={'--current_week':'cw','--last_week':'lw','--today':'T','--yesterday':'Y','--date <DATE>':'D','--from <FROM_DATE>':'F','--to <TO_DATE>':'X'}
    rows.append((order,inv[m.group(1)],inv[m.group(2)]))
PRI=['F','X','D','T','Y','cw','lw']
def cf(a,s):
    return {x for x in s if x!=a and PRI.index(x)>PRI.index(a)} | ({'X'} if a=='F' and 'X' in s else set())
def pickA(s):
    for a in PRI:
        if a in s and cf(a,s): return a
    return None
rules={
 'nextpos_wrap': lambda a,order: order[(order.index(a)+1)%len(order)],
 'prevpos_wrap': lambda a,order: order[(order.index(a)-1)%len(order)],
 'closest': lambda a,order: min([x for x in order if x in cf(a,order)], key=lambda x: min(abs(order.index(x)-order.index(a)), len(order)-abs(order.index(x)-order.index(a)))),
 'closest_then_first': lambda a,order: sorted([x for x in order if x in cf(a,order)], key=lambda x:(min(abs(order.index(x)-order.index(a)), len(order)-abs(order.index(x)-order.index(a))), order.index(x)))[0],
 'prev_conf': lambda a,order: next((x for x in reversed(order[:order.index(a)]) if x in cf(a,order)), None) or next((x for x in order[order.index(a)+1:] if x in cf(a,order)),None),
 'next_conf_then_prev': lambda a,order: (next((x for x in order[order.index(a)+1:] if x in cf(a,order)),None) or next((x for x in reversed(order[:order.index(a)]) if x in cf(a,order)),None)),
 'last_before_then_after': lambda a,order: (next((x for x in reversed(order[:order.index(a)]) if x in cf(a,order)),None) or next((x for x in order[order.index(a)+1:] if x in cf(a,order)),None)),
}
for name,fn in rules.items():
    ok=0;bad=0
    for order,a,b in rows:
        if a is None: continue
        try: m=fn(a,order)
        except Exception: m=None
        if m==b: ok+=1
        else: bad+=1
    print(ok,bad,name)
PY

cd /tmp/bt && python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess, os, datetime, re
LOG="/tmp/bt/rr.txt"
lines=[]
for i in range(200):
    lines.append("2026-11-%02d %02d:00 | P%d | d%d" % (1+i%25, 8+(i//25), i%7, i))
open(LOG,'w').write("\n".join(lines)+"\n")
env=dict(os.environ); env["BARTIB_FILE"]=LOG
# run both in parallel
import threading
res={}
def f(b,k):
    r=subprocess.run([b,"report"],capture_output=True,env=env)
    res[k]=r.stdout.decode()
t1=threading.Thread(target=f,args=("/workspace/executable","o")); t2=threading.Thread(target=f,args=("/tmp/cmp/executable","m"))
t1.start(); t2.start(); t1.join(); t2.join()
def tot(out):
    out=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',out)
    m=re.search(r'Total\.*\s*(\d+)h (\d+)m', out)
    return int(m.group(1))*60+int(m.group(2))
now=datetime.datetime.now(); secs=int(now.timestamp())
starts=[]
for i in range(200):
    starts.append(int(datetime.datetime(2026,11,1+i%25, 8+(i//25),0).timestamp()))
trunc=sum((secs-s)//60 for s in starts)
print("now", now, "ORIG", tot(res['o']), "MINE", tot(res['m']), "exp_trunc", trunc, "diff_o", tot(res['o'])-trunc, "diff_m", tot(res['m'])-trunc)
PY

import subprocess, os, datetime, re, threading
import datetime as dt
LOG="/tmp/cmp/log.txt"
lines=[]
for i in range(200):
    lines.append("2026-11-%02d %02d:00 | P%d | d%d" % (1+i%25, 8+(i//25), i%7, i))
content="\n".join(lines)+"\n"
def runp(b, content, args):
    open(LOG,'w').write(content)
    env=dict(os.environ); env["BARTIB_FILE"]=LOG
    r=subprocess.run([b]+args,capture_output=True,env=env)
    return r.stdout.decode()
def tot(out):
    out=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',out)
    m=re.search(r'Total\.*\s*(?:<1m|(\d+)h (\d+)m)', out)
    return int(m.group(1))*60+int(m.group(2)) if m and m.group(1) else None
for trial in range(2):
    res={}
    t0=datetime.datetime.now(); secs=int(t0.timestamp())
    ts=[threading.Thread(target=lambda k,b: res.update({k: runp(b,content,["report"])}), args=(k,b)) for k,b in (("o","/workspace/executable"),("m","/tmp/cmp/executable"))]
    for t in ts: t.start()
    for t in ts: t.join()
    starts=[int(dt.datetime(2026,11,1+i%25, 8+(i//25),0).timestamp()) for i in range(200)]
    raw=sum(secs-s for s in starts)
    trunc=sum((secs-s)//60 for s in starts)
    print("now=%s ORIG %s MINE %s raw/60 %d trunc %d" % (t0.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), tot(res['o']), tot(res['m']), raw//60, trunc))
PY

# bartib re-implementation

Rust reimplementation of `bartib` 1.1.0 (a command line time tracker).
No external crates are used; the date/time handling, the `clap`-style CLI and
all output formatting were re-implemented from scratch.

## Layout
* `src/datetime.rs` â proleptic Gregorian date/time, chrono compatible
  parsing errors (`input is out of range`, `input contains invalid characters`,
  `premature end of input`, `trailing input`).
* `src/activity.rs` â log file parsing (incl. second-precision timestamps and
  the leap-second `:60` quirk) and file writing.
* `src/cli.rs` â clap 2.x style parsing, help rendering and error messages.
* `src/commands.rs` â all sub commands.
* `src/render.rs` â NBSP padding, ANSI colours, duration formatting,
  `--round` parsing.
* `compile.sh` â `cargo build --offline --release` and copies the binary to
  `./executable` (removing the read-only reference binary first).

## Verified behaviour (compared byte for byte against the original)
help/version output for all sub commands, clap error messages (unknown
argument, missing value, duplicate, conflicts, missing required), list/report/
last/search/current/projects/status/sanity/check output and colouring,
grouping rules, week starting Monday, status only counting up to today,
start/stop/cancel/change/continue file rewriting (blank lines and unparsable
lines preserved), `-t` time parsing warnings, `--round` parsing quirks
(single digit silently ignored, invalid unit warns, unit must be `m`/`h`),
log parsing edge cases (`|`, empty description/project, extra segments,
invalid UTF-8 stops reading, directory silently yields no activities).

## Known limitations / open items
* Durations of running activities are aggregated from the raw second
  precision values and truncated at the end (matching the original).  With a
  log containing many *running* activities the total can differ by a minute
  or two when the compared runs fall on either side of a second boundary;
  running both binaries in parallel produces identical output, so this is a
  measurement artefact of the test harness rather than a behavioural gap.
* Three-way conflict error messages (e.g. `list --today --yesterday
  --current_week`) use a fixed priority order for the reported pair which
  matches two-way conflicts and most, but not all, three-way combinations.
* `--round ""` (empty argument) reproduces the original panic but the panic
  message contains this project's source location instead of the Rust
  standard library path.
EOF
git add -A && git status --short | head -20"}

Rust reimplementation of `bartib` 1.1.0 (a command line time tracker).
No external crates are used; the date/time handling, the `clap`-style CLI and
all output formatting were re-implemented from scratch.

## Layout
* `src/datetime.rs` â proleptic Gregorian date/time, chrono compatible
  parsing errors (`input is out of range`, `input contains invalid characters`,
  `premature end of input`, `trailing input`).
* `src/activity.rs` â log file parsing (incl. second-precision timestamps and
  the leap-second `:60` quirk) and file writing.
* `src/cli.rs` â clap 2.x style parsing, help rendering and error messages.
* `src/commands.rs` â all sub commands.
* `src/render.rs` â NBSP padding, ANSI colours, duration formatting,
  `--round` parsing.
* `compile.sh` â `cargo build --offline --release` and copies the binary to
  `./executable` (removing the read-only reference binary first).

## Verified behaviour (compared byte for byte against the original)
help/version output for all sub commands, clap error messages (unknown
argument, missing value, duplicate, conflicts, missing required), list/report/
last/search/current/projects/status/sanity/check output and colouring,
grouping rules, week starting Monday, status only counting up to today,
start/stop/cancel/change/continue file rewriting (blank lines and unparsable
lines preserved), `-t` time parsing warnings, `--round` parsing quirks
(single digit silently ignored, invalid unit warns, unit must be `m`/`h`),
log parsing edge cases (`|`, empty description/project, extra segments,
invalid UTF-8 stops reading, directory silently yields no activities).

## Known limitations / open items
* Durations of running activities are aggregated from the raw second
  precision values and truncated at the end (matching the original).  With a
  log containing many *running* activities the total can differ by a minute
  or two when the compared runs fall on either side of a second boundary;
  running both binaries in parallel produces identical output, so this is a
  measurement artefact of the test harness rather than a behavioural gap.
* Three-way conflict error messages (e.g. `list --today --yesterday
  --current_week`) use a fixed priority order for the reported pair which
  matches two-way conflicts and most, but not all, three-way combinations.
* `--round ""` (empty argument) reproduces the original panic but the panic
  message contains this project's source location instead of the Rust
  standard library path.
EOF
